transcript.text: Shark NZ801UK anti hair wrap upright - suction has gone really weak over the last couple of weeks, barely picks up crumbs. Have emptied the bin. Any ideas before I buy a new one?

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. Yes, hold off buying a new one for now. Suction that fades over a couple of weeks, even with the bin emptied, is almost always an airflow problem rather than the motor failing, and it's usually free to fix. 1. Clogged filters. Shark uprights typically have a foam and felt pre-motor filter under the bin and a HEPA filter elsewhere on the body. Fine dust builds up in these gradually, which matches the slow decline you've had.
2. A blockage somewhere in the airflow path: hose, wand, floorhead neck or bin inlet. Crumbs, a sock or a wad of fluff can lodge there and choke it.
3. An air leak from a split hose or a bin or lid not seated properly. 1. Filters: take out the pre-motor filters (usually under the bin lid or behind the dust cup) and the HEPA filter. Leave them to dry fully for at least 24 hours, because a damp filter chokes airflow too. If they come out grey and caked, that's very likely your culprit.
2. Blockages: detach the hose and wand and look through each one. A coin dropped through should fall straight out. Check the neck where the floorhead joins and the opening into the bin too. If you find a clog, clear it; that alone often brings full suction back.
3. Seals and hose: while you're there, check the hose for splits (flex it along its length) and make sure the bin clicks firmly into place. With dry filters and a clear path, test it on a hard floor. If suction is back, that was it. If it's still weak after all that, the next suspects are a blocked cyclone section inside the bin assembly or a perished seal, and the bin assembly is sometimes available as a separate part. A genuinely failing motor is less common and usually sounds different, with a whining or burning smell. At that point it's worth weighing a repair against the machine's age. Let me know what the filters and hose look like once you've had a go.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

Found foam and felt filters under the bin, never washed them. Foam one is solid grey, the felt is caked with fine dust. Coin goes straight through the hose, no splits, and the bin seal looks fine. No burning smell either, motor sounds normal.

That's probably your answer. A solid grey foam filter and a caked felt one will choke the airflow badly, and filters that have never been washed fit perfectly with suction fading gradually over a couple of weeks. With a clear hose, sound seals and a normal-sounding motor with no burning smell, there's nothing pointing at the motor. 1. Wash the foam and felt filters in cold water only, with no soap or detergent. The felt may stay a bit discoloured, and that's fine.
2. Leave them to air-dry for at least 24 hours, ideally longer, somewhere warm but not on a radiator or in a dryer. Refit them only when they're bone dry.
3. While they dry, find the post-motor (HEPA) filter. On Shark uprights it's typically behind a grille or cover on the body. If it's grey and dusty, tap it out over a bin. Many are rinsable too, so check the label or manual before getting it wet.
4. Turn the floorhead over and make sure the brush bar turns freely by hand.
5. Refit everything, check the bin clicks home, and test it on a hard floor. If suction comes back strongly, that was it. Wash the filters every month or so from now on to stop it happening again. If the foam has torn or crumbled, or the filters won't come reasonably clean, the filter itself is the likely part at fault. If everything is clean and dry and it's still weak, the next suspect is a blocked cyclone section in the bin assembly. Let me know how it goes.
Ok, washed both in lukewarm water and left them 24 hours to dry. Massive difference, suction is back to like new. Brushroll spins freely too, just a bit of fluff on it.

Brilliant, that's sorted, and no need for a new vacuum. Never-washed filters that had gone solid grey and caked were choking the airflow, and cleaning them has brought it back to like new. To stop it creeping back:
1. Rinse the foam and felt filters roughly once a month, more often if you have pets or it gets heavy use. Use plain water and let them dry fully, at least 24 hours, before refitting.
2. Tap out or rinse the post-motor (HEPA) filter every few months if it's the washable type.
3. Empty the bin before it reaches the max line.
4. Pick that bit of fluff off the brush roll every so often. If suction ever drops again soon after a wash, or the foam starts to tear or crumble, a replacement filter set is cheap and worth fitting. Anything else I can help with?
